title: kate-session: drop the paths that match an exclude pattern
summary: compile_excludes turns the exclude_patterns strings into regexes and reports a bad pattern. is_excluded says whether a relative path, written with forward slashes, matches any of them anywhere, the way QRegularExpression::match does in Kate.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. The crate is pure Rust and builds anywhere. The backlog marks this title LOCAL so the Mac lane keeps the panes and their models together.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Both functions carry #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))] until Project::files calls them. A pattern that regex::Regex::new rejects is ProjectError::Pattern with the pattern and the error text. is_excluded uses Regex::is_match. The test exclude_patterns_match_anywhere compiles ["^target/", "\\.o$"] and asserts target/debug/x is excluded, src/target/x is not, main.o is excluded, and main.rs is not; a pattern ( is Err(Pattern). Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: exclude::tests::exclude_patterns_match_anywhere
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because the functions do not exist. After the change the anchored pattern excludes only a leading target and a bad pattern is a Pattern error.
